description: The bar chart compares the accuracy (%) of a model across two datasets, PHME and PolitiFact, under different experimental conditions. On the left, the PHME dataset shows accuracy values for five conditions: "Ours" (89.84%), "w/o comments" (86.82%), "w/o text" (80.10%), "w/o select" (88.80%), "w/o emotion" (87.34%), and "w/o cognition" (87.17%). The "Ours" condition achieves the highest accuracy, followed by "w/o select," while "w/o text" has the lowest. On the right, the PolitiFact dataset shows similar conditions with accuracy values: "Ours" (90.57%), "w/o comments" (85.85%), "w/o text" (83.02%), "w/o select" (89.62%), "w/o emotion" (84.91%), and "w/o cognition" (87.74%). Here, "Ours" again achieves the highest accuracy, followed by "w/o select," while "w/o text" has the lowest. In both datasets, the "Ours" condition outperforms all other conditions, and the "w/o text" condition consistently results in the lowest accuracy. The bars are color-coded, with "Ours" in dark red, "w/o comments" in orange, "w/o text" in light yellow, "w/o select" in light blue, "w/o emotion" in medium blue, and "w/o cognition" in dark blue. The y-axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 75.0 to 95.0, with a linear scale. The x-axis lists the conditions, and the bars are sorted in descending order of accuracy for each dataset. The chart is divided by a vertical dashed line, separating the two datasets.
